question: How long would a FULL exhaustive nibble search on GPU take at m=37?
method: Measured the COMPLETE (no-budget, deterministic) DFS search-tree node count for the k=0 permutation slice at m=3..12, fit nodes(m)~c*r^m log-linearly on m=7..12, extrapolated to m=37. Multiplied by the number of 2-factor type multisets for the full space.
note_sols: k=0 permutation slice has NO solution for m>=6 (real rot4 solutions are non-permutation 2-factors). This slice is the SMALLEST of all types => strict lower bound on the tree.

fit.caveat: r drifts upward with m (top-of-tree branching ~ m), so extrapolation is a mild UNDER-estimate

verdict: Full exhaustive GPU nibble is astronomically infeasible: ~1e24 yr (current code) to ~1e20 yr (idealized perfect GPU) = 10^10 to 10^14 times the age of the universe. Even the smallest solution-free slice needs ~40M yr (current) / ~3400 yr (ideal). This is why we use randomized nibble + SAT (smart pruning), never brute force.
